title: Driver coverage gaps — M1–M5 audit findings
source: Post-M5 audit of drivers against SPECIFICATION.md §11 (milestone properties) and §12 (driver catalogue). Gaps identified by comparing each driver's scenarios against the spec's 'Exercises' and 'What you learn' claims for that layer.

baseline.notes:
M5 is complete. All existing drivers pass. This plan addresses scenarios that are absent from drivers but explicitly required or implied by the spec. Gaps are grouped by severity: Epoch 0 is on the M6 critical path (should_stop_after_turn is called by the compaction hook); Epoch 1 fills in the M4 driver claims the spec makes but aren't demonstrated; Epoch 2 is low-priority polish.

GAPS FOUND:
(M2) loop_driver: should_stop_after_turn, before_tool_call, after_tool_call, prepare_next_turn, transform_context hooks are entirely untested. Spec says 'The full turn-and-hook surface is exercised.' Only get_steering_messages and get_follow_up_messages are covered.
(M2) loop_driver: thinking blocks (AME_thinking_start, AME_thinking_delta, AThinking content) never appear in any Faux_provider script.
(M5) session_driver: 'fsync ordering survives a kill -9' is listed in the spec driver catalogue as what session_driver validates. No scenario exists. The practical test is crash-resilience: write N fsync'd entries, then append a partial line to the file (simulating a crash mid-write), verify the reader rejects the partial line while preserving the valid entries.
(M4) env_driver: only exercises shell (Sh.*) operations. Spec says 'Local_env filesystem and shell operations one at a time.' No Fs.* scenarios exist; covered only by unit tests, not the driver.
(M4) tool_driver: spec says 'Schema validation, truncation, output formatting.' No truncation scenario; no invalid-args scenario.
(M1) provider_driver: thinking blocks never exercised against the real Anthropic API.
(M3) No isolated provider-layer smoke test for the OpenAI completions SSE wire format.

epochs.title: M6 critical path — loop hooks + session crash resilience
epochs.description: The two highest-severity gaps. should_stop_after_turn is the hook compaction will use to exit the inner loop; without a driver scenario it is unvalidated on the M6 critical path. The session_driver crash-resilience scenario is the spec's stated evidence for the M5 durability claim.

stages.title: loop_driver — full hook surface coverage
stages.description: Add six scenarios to loop_driver covering every untested hook in agent_loop_config. Uses Faux_provider.recorded_contexts to verify transform_context. Uses the existing run_scenario helper pattern.
stages.implementation_notes:
Add the following scenarios after scenario_follow_up_message, before run_all_scenarios.

SCENARIO 8 — should_stop_after_turn_halts_loop:
Provide a 2-turn Faux script (turn 1: text reply EndTurn; turn 2: text reply EndTurn).
Configure should_stop_after_turn to return true after seeing 1 AE_turn_end.
Verify: only 1 turn_start event fires; AE_agent_end is the last event; second Faux script turn is never consumed (Faux_provider raises Failure if over-consumed, so no extra assertion needed).
Implementation:
  let stop_count = ref 0 in
  let should_stop_after_turn = Some (fun _ctx ->
    incr stop_count;
    Int.equal !stop_count 1) in
  let config = make_config ~should_stop_after_turn stream_fn in
  check: count_events is_turn_start events = 1 && check_agent_end_is_last events.

SCENARIO 9 — before_tool_call_allow:
Script a single echo tool call (ToolUse stop + follow-up EndTurn).
before_tool_call returns Allow.
Verify: tool executes (AE_tool_execution_end with is_error=false), loop completes normally.

SCENARIO 10 — before_tool_call_deny:
Same script.
before_tool_call returns Deny "blocked by policy".
Verify: AE_tool_execution_end fires with is_error=true; the tool result content contains "blocked by policy"; loop continues (follow-up turn runs) and AE_agent_end fires.

SCENARIO 11 — after_tool_call_fires:
Script a single echo tool call.
after_tool_call records each invocation (ref list of tool_call.id).
Verify: after send, the recorded list has exactly 1 entry matching the echo tool call id.

SCENARIO 12 — transform_context_applied:
Script a single text turn (no tools).
transform_context appends a known synthetic agent_message (Agent_types.Real (UserMessage {role='user'; content=[UText 'INJECTED']}) to the messages before each LLM call.
After run_scenario, call Faux_provider.recorded_contexts () and verify the first context's messages list contains a message with content text 'INJECTED'.
Note: reset_recorded() at start of scenario.

SCENARIO 13 — prepare_next_turn_update:
Script 2 turns: turn 1 EndTurn, turn 2 EndTurn. Use should_stop_after_turn=None so both turns run.
prepare_next_turn returns Some (Agent_types.{ messages=None; model=Some {id='prepared-model'; api='faux'}; thinking=None }).
After run, call recorded_contexts () and verify the second context's model_id is 'prepared-model'.
Note: Agent_types.turn_update is { messages: agent_message list option; model: model option; thinking: bool option }. Check the actual field names from agent_types.mli.

Add all 6 to run_all_scenarios and run_named_scenario match.

NOTE on Agent_types.turn_update: verify the exact record structure in agent_types.mli before implementing scenario 13. If the field is model_override or similar, use the actual name.

NOTE on before_tool_call Deny: the loop converts a Deny result to a tool result with is_error=true. Check agent_loop.ml around line 261 to confirm the exact error text plumbing so the content check is precise.

test-patterns.md — driver exercises public interface; one scenario per claim

new_tests: before_tool_call_deny: tool is_error=true, deny message in result

stages.title: session_driver — crash-resilience / fsync scenario
stages.description: Add a 'crash_resilience' scenario to session_driver that validates the spec claim: 'A process crash mid-write may leave a partial line, which a future reader rejects; otherwise the file is well-formed up to the last completed entry.' This is the observable evidence for 'fsync ordering survives a kill -9' in the spec's driver catalogue — the invariant being demonstrated is that every completed (fsync'd) write is readable, and a partial trailing write does not corrupt the previously-fsync'd entries.
stages.implementation_notes:
ADD to session_jsonl_helpers:

(** Parse a session file tolerating a partial last line. Returns only the
    lines that parse as valid JSON; skips lines that raise an exception. *)
val parse_session_file_lenient : string -> Yojson.Safe.t list

Implementation in session_jsonl_helpers.ml:
let parse_session_file_lenient path =
  let contents = Stdlib.In_channel.(with_open_text path input_all) in
  let lines = String.split_on_char '\n' contents in
  let nonempty = List.filter (fun s -> not (String.is_empty s)) lines in
  List.filter_map (fun line ->
    try Some (Yojson.Safe.from_string line)
    with _ -> None) nonempty

ADD to session_driver.ml:

SCENARIO 6 — crash_resilience:
Step 1: create a Session_writer, call write_session_info + write_message (user) + write_message (assistant) + write_leaf. These 4 entries are each fsync'd before returning.
Step 2: re-open the file and append a partial/malformed line (simulating a crash mid-write before fsync):
  let oc = Stdlib.Out_channel.open_gen [Open_append; Open_binary] 0o644 path in
  Stdlib.Out_channel.output_string oc "{\"id\":\"partial-line-no-closing";
  Stdlib.Out_channel.close oc
Step 3: call parse_session_file_lenient path.
Step 4: verify:
  (a) exactly 4 valid entries are returned (the partial line is skipped)
  (b) verify_chain_and_leaves on those 4 entries returns Pass (tree structure intact)
  (c) types are [session_info; message; message; leaf] in order

NOTE: write_session_info must be called before write_message (it initialises the session and sets the parent chain). The 4 entries are: SessionInfo, UserMessage, AssistantMessage, Leaf.

PRINT output: '[session] crash_resilience ... PASS' or FAIL with reason.
Add to the scenarios list in main so it prints with the others and is counted.

This scenario directly demonstrates the spec invariant without requiring Unix.fork or SIGKILL: the 4 entries written via Session_writer (each with Eio.File.sync) survive the subsequent append of a partial line, and the lenient reader recovers the intact tree.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: test-patterns.md — scenario documents its invariant in a comment

test_requirements.notes: parse_session_file_lenient is a new export from session_jsonl_helpers. The existing parse_session_file remains unchanged (it uses from_string which raises on invalid JSON, appropriate for normal use). The lenient variant is only needed here.

stages.title: env_driver — filesystem operation scenarios
stages.description: Add Fs.* scenarios to env_driver covering the filesystem half of Local_env. The spec's driver catalogue says env_driver exercises 'Local_env filesystem and shell operations one at a time.' Currently only shell operations are covered.
stages.implementation_notes:
Add the following scenarios to env_driver. Each uses the existing (module E : Execution_env.S) pattern. The tmpdir is already created by make_temp_dir.

SCENARIO 6 — fs_write_read:
  let module E = ... in
  (match E.Fs.write_file ~path:"hello.txt" ~content:"hello world" with
  | Error e -> Fail ...
  | Ok () ->
    match E.Fs.read_file ~path:"hello.txt" with
    | Error e -> Fail ...
    | Ok content ->
      if String.equal (String.trim content) "hello world" then Pass
      else Fail ...)

SCENARIO 7 — fs_file_exists:
  Write "exists.txt", verify E.Fs.file_exists ~path:"exists.txt" = true.
  Verify E.Fs.file_exists ~path:"nonexistent.txt" = false.

SCENARIO 8 — fs_list_dir:
  Write two files "a.txt" and "b.txt" in tmpdir.
  E.Fs.list_dir ~path:"." -> verify result contains both filenames.

SCENARIO 9 — fs_read_nonexistent:
  E.Fs.read_file ~path:"no_such_file.txt" -> verify result is Error with code NotFound (or equivalent).
  Check Pera_types.Types.equal_file_error_code e.code NotFound.

SCENARIO 10 — fs_write_creates_parent_dirs (optional, skip if not supported):
  E.Fs.write_file ~path:"subdir/nested.txt" ~content:"x" -> if Ok, verify file exists.
  If Error (mkdir not supported), Skip with reason.

Add all to run_scenarios list. Count Skips separately.

NOTE: Check the actual Execution_env.S Fs module interface in lib/pera_env/execution_env.mli for exact function signatures (read_file, write_file, file_exists, list_dir). The error type may be file_error or execution_error; use the right comparison.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pera-specific.md — IO functions return Result, never raise

stages.title: tool_driver — truncation and invalid-args scenarios
stages.description: Add two scenarios to tool_driver: one verifying output truncation on large files (the spec says 'truncation, output formatting'), one verifying graceful error on invalid/missing args (the spec says 'schema validation').
stages.implementation_notes:
SCENARIO 8 — read_truncation:
Write a file with content larger than the read tool's truncation limit. The read tool uses Pera_tools.Truncate; check truncate.mli for the default limit (likely ~8000 chars or similar).
Write a file with 20000 'x' characters.
Read it via the read tool.
Verify the output:
  (a) is shorter than the input (truncation occurred)
  (b) contains a truncation marker (check Truncate for the exact marker string — likely something like '[... truncated]' or similar)

SCENARIO 9 — read_missing_path_arg:
Call read.execute ~ctx:() ~args:(`Assoc []) ~sw ~cancel (no 'path' key).
Verify: result is Error e and e.message is non-empty.
This demonstrates that the tool handles missing required arguments gracefully without raising.

Note on schema validation: schema validation (Json_schema coercion) happens in the agent loop, not in tool.execute. The tool.execute receives pre-coerced args. 'Invalid args' at the tool level means the tool does its own defensive arg extraction — read_tool extracts 'path' with a fallback. The test should pass empty args and confirm the tool returns a sensible error rather than raising or panicking.

Check Pera_tools.Truncate for the actual max output size and marker string before writing the scenario, to avoid hardcoding the wrong values.

Add both to the Eio.Cancel.sub verdicts list in main.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: naming-and-intermediates.md — name the truncation limit constant

new_tests: read_truncation: output shorter than input and contains truncation marker
read_missing_path_arg: returns Error with non-empty message
test_requirements.notes: Check Pera_tools.Truncate.max_output_chars or equivalent for the exact limit. The marker string is in truncate.ml.

acceptance_criteria: dune build passes

stages.title: loop_driver — thinking block scenario
stages.description: Add a scenario where the Faux_provider emits AME_thinking_start + AME_thinking_delta events and the final message contains AThinking content. Validates that thinking blocks flow through the loop correctly and appear in AE_message_end.
stages.implementation_notes:
SCENARIO 14 — thinking_blocks:
Build a Faux turn where events include:
  AME_thinking_start { partial = partial_msg }
  AME_thinking_delta { text = "thinking step"; partial = partial_msg }
  AME_text_start { partial = partial_msg }
  AME_text_delta { text = "answer"; partial = final_msg }
The final_msg has content = [ AThinking { text="thinking step"; signature=None }; AText "answer" ].
Verify:
  (a) AE_message_end fires with a message containing AThinking content
  (b) AE_agent_end is last

Check: List.exists (function
  | AE_message_end { message = Real (AssistantMessage am) } ->
      List.exists (function AThinking _ -> true | _ -> false) am.content
  | _ -> false) events
